claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do! I'm inquiring about my child Alex. He's 8 years old and lives with me here at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's helpful to know that Alex is 8 years old and lives with you at home.

To continue assessing your eligibility, I need to ask: **Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Now I need to ask: **Are you responsible for Alex's care and upkeep? For example, do you provide for his food, clothes, accommodation, and other daily needs?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I'm responsible for Alex - I provide all his food, clothes, and everything he needs day to day.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent. Now I need to ask: **Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. A few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is Alex currently in hospital, care, or residential accommodation for an extended period, or does he live at home with you full-time?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually, I'm fostering Alex. He lives with me at home full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that important information. Since you're fostering Alex, I need to ask: **Is the local council paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure about that, to be honest. I don't know if the council pays towards his accommodation or maintenance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Let me explain why this is important: If you're fostering Alex, you can still get Child Benefit for him, **as long as the local council is not paying anything towards his accommodation or maintenance**. If the council is providing financial support for these costs, it would affect your eligibility.

I'd recommend checking with your local council or reviewing any fostering agreements you have to clarify whether they're paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance costs.

In the meantime, let me ask: **Are there any other circumstances I should know about? For example, does Alex have any other living arrangements, or are there any other factors that might affect your claim?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, there's nothing else - Alex just lives with me at home full-time, and that's the situation. He's only 8, so he's not working or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me summarize what we've discussed:

- Alex is 8 years old and lives with you full-time in the UK
- You are responsible for his care and provide for all his needs
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him
- You are fostering Alex
- You're unsure whether the local council pays towards his accommodation or maintenance

Based on the eligibility rules, the key determining factor for your situation is whether the local council is paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance. 

**If the council is NOT paying towards his accommodation or maintenance**, you would be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

**If the council IS paying towards his accommodation or maintenance**, you would not be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Since you're uncertain about the council payments, I cannot make a definitive determination of your eligibility at this time. I would recommend:

1. Checking with your local council or fostering agency about whether they pay towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance
2. Once you have that information, you can contact the Child Benefit Office directly, or come back with that detail

Would you like to find out this information and let me know, or would you like me to provide a determination based on what we know so far?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
I understand. So just to be clear - if the council isn't paying anything towards his accommodation or maintenance, then I would be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex? And if they are paying, then I wouldn't be eligible?

I'll need to check with the fostering agency to find out for certain. Is there anything else I need to know or any other information that might affect my eligibility?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Yes, that's correct! To confirm:

- **If the council is NOT paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance** → You would be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex
- **If the council IS paying towards his accommodation or maintenance** → You would not be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex

Based on all the information you've provided, that's the only outstanding factor that would affect your eligibility for Alex. Everything else about your situation meets the eligibility criteria:

✓ Alex is under 16
✓ You live in the UK
✓ Alex lives with you full-time
✓ You're responsible for his care and provide for his needs
✓ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him
✓ He's not in hospital or care

So once you check with your fostering agency about whether the council pays towards his accommodation or maintenance, you'll have your answer about eligibility.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit or the application process?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I think that's everything I needed to know. Thank you for explaining it so clearly - I'll check with the fostering agency about the council payments and then I'll know whether I can claim. I appreciate your help!

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help clarify the situation for you.

Just to recap: once you confirm with your fostering agency whether the council is paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance, you'll know definitively whether you're eligible. If they're not paying anything towards those costs, you should be able to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

Best of luck with checking that information, and I hope everything works out well for you and Alex. Take care!

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Thank you so much! Take care.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're welcome! Take care and all the best! 

If you have any other questions after speaking with the fostering agency, feel free to come back. Goodbye!

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Thank you, goodbye!

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Goodbye! 😊
